questions.question: Which of the following soils is most suitable for rice cultivation in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Alluvial soil**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Alluvial soil** is the most suitable soil for rice cultivation due to its **fertility and moisture retention capacity**.
 
• It is rich in essential nutrients such as **potash, phosphoric acid, and lime**, which are required for the growth of rice plants.
 
• Alluvial soils are formed by the deposition of sediments brought by rivers such as the **Ganga, Brahmaputra, and Indus**.
 
• This soil type is widely found in the **Indo-Gangetic plain**, which is a major rice-growing region in India.
 
• It has a **clayey texture** that helps retain water, a crucial factor for rice cultivation as rice requires standing water during its growth phase.
 
• Alluvial soil is found in **low-lying areas** that are naturally irrigated by river systems, making it ideal for rice farming.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Desert Soil**__

 __
 
• **Desert soil** is found in arid regions such as **Rajasthan** and is characterized by low fertility and high sand content.
 
• It lacks moisture and organic content, making it unsuitable for rice cultivation.
 
• This soil type is typically used for crops that require minimal water, such as **millets and pulses**.
 
 
 
• **Red Soil**__
 __
 
• **Red soil** is found in regions such as **Chhattisgarh, Tamil Nadu, and Karnataka**.
 
• It is formed by the weathering of crystalline rocks and is rich in **iron oxide**, giving it a reddish color.
 
• Although it is fertile for crops like **groundnut, cotton, and millets**, it lacks essential nutrients such as nitrogen and organic matter, making it less suitable for rice cultivation.
 
 
 
• **Saline Soil**__
 
 
• **Saline soil** is characterized by high salt content and is found in areas such as **Rann of Kutch in Gujarat and coastal regions**.
 
• It is not suitable for most crops, including rice, due to its **poor drainage and high salinity**.
 
• Efforts are often required to reclaim saline soils for agricultural use.

questions.question: What is the unit of measurement for frequenсу?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Hertz (Hz)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Hertz (Hz)** is the **SI unit of frequency**, which measures the number of cycles of a periodic wave per second.
 
• It is named after the German physicist **Heinrich Rudolf Hertz**, who made significant contributions to the understanding of electromagnetic waves.
 
• 1 Hertz represents **one cycle per second**. For example, a frequency of 50 Hz means there are 50 cycles of the wave occurring each second.
 
• The unit is widely used in various fields such as **physics, telecommunications, acoustics, and electronics** to describe the frequency of waves, including sound waves, electromagnetic waves, and alternating current.
 
• Applications of frequency measurement in **Hertz** include **radio broadcasting** (e.g., FM radio operates at 88-108 MHz), **electricity** (standard power supply frequency is 50 Hz or 60 Hz), and **digital systems** (e.g., processor clock speeds in GHz).
 
• The **Hertz** is a derived unit, and its dimensional formula is **T⁻¹**, where T represents time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Millisecond**__

 __
 
• A **millisecond** (ms) is a unit of time and is equal to **one-thousandth of a second** (1 ms = 0.001 seconds).
 
• It is commonly used in fields like **computer science** and **electronics** to measure short time intervals, such as **response times**.
 
 
 
• **Pascal**__
 __
 
• The **Pascal (Pa)** is the SI unit of **pressure**, not frequency.
 
• It is defined as **one newton per square meter** (1 Pa = 1 N/m²).
 
• This unit is used to measure pressure in various fields such as **fluid dynamics, meteorology, and material science**.
 
 
 
• **Joule**__
 
 
• The **Joule (J)** is the SI unit of **energy**, not frequency.
 
• It is defined as the **work done** when a force of one newton moves an object one meter (1 J = 1 N·m).
 
• It is used in fields like **physics, engineering, and thermodynamics** to measure energy, work, or heat.

questions.question: Which of the following conditions will prevent a file from being renamed in a Windows-based operating system?

options.text: The file has a long name exceeding 255 characters.
The file is located in the Recycle Bin.
The file has the 'Read-only' attribute enabled.
The file is currently opened in another application.

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**The file is currently opened in another application.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In a **Windows-based operating system**, a file cannot be renamed if it is currently **opened in another application.**
 
• This is because the operating system locks the file to prevent any modifications while it is in use, ensuring **data integrity** and avoiding conflicts.
 
• Applications that open files typically place a lock on them, preventing other processes from renaming, editing, or deleting the file.
 
• For example, if a document is opened in **Microsoft Word**, the file cannot be renamed until the application is closed.
 
• Such restrictions help maintain the stability and functionality of the operating system by avoiding potential errors or corruption.
 
• To rename a file in this scenario, users must ensure that the file is **closed in all running applications.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

 __
 
• In **Windows operating systems**, file names are limited to a maximum of **255 characters** including the file path.
 
• Exceeding this limit can result in errors when attempting to open, rename, or perform any operation on the file.
 
• Such files may require specialized tools or techniques to be renamed or accessed.
 
 
 
• **The file is located in the Recycle Bin**__
 __
 
• Files in the **Recycle Bin** are considered temporarily deleted and cannot be renamed directly.
 
• To rename such files, they must first be **restored** to their original location.
 
• The **Recycle Bin** is a feature in Windows that allows users to recover accidentally deleted files.
 
 
 
• **The file has the 'Read-only' attribute enabled**__
 
 
• A file with the **'Read-only'** attribute is protected from being modified or deleted but can still be renamed.
 
• The 'Read-only' status can be removed by accessing the file's **Properties** in Windows.
 
• This attribute is often used to safeguard important files from unintended changes.

• Users can also use AutoFill for copying formulas across a range of cells, which dynamically adjusts references based on the relative position of cells.

• The **Board of Control** was established under the **Pitt's India Act of 1784**.
 
• This act was introduced to ensure better governance of the **British territories in India**.
 
• The board had the authority to oversee and direct all matters related to the **civil and military government** in British India.
 
• It functioned alongside the **Court of Directors of the East India Company**, ensuring a balance between the British Crown and the Company.
 
• The Board of Control consisted of **six members**, including the **Chancellor of the Exchequer** and the **Secretary of State**.

• Each corner atom is shared among **8 adjacent unit cells**, while the central atom belongs entirely to the unit cell.
 
• The coordination number of 8 arises from the geometry of the lattice, where the central atom is equidistant from the 8 corner atoms.
 
• This arrangement is commonly found in metals like **iron, chromium, and tungsten**, which adopt the BCC structure.
 
• The BCC lattice is less densely packed compared to other structures like **face-centered cubic (FCC)** or **hexagonal close-packed (HCP)**, but it provides good mechanical stability.

• **Relative Reference** in MS Excel adjusts both the **column letter** and **row number** automatically when a formula is copied to another location.
 
• This type of reference is extremely useful when creating formulas that need to be applied across multiple rows or columns dynamically.
 
• For example, if you use a formula like **=A1+B1** in a cell and copy it to another location, the formula will automatically adjust to **=A2+B2**, **=A3+B3**, and so on.
 
• **Relative references** are the default reference type in MS Excel unless explicitly changed.
 
• They save time and effort by eliminating the need to manually rewrite formulas for different cells.
 
• Relative references are denoted without any **$** symbols, e.g., **A1**.
 
• This type of reference is widely used in scenarios such as **data analysis, calculations, and creating dynamic tables**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Static Reference**__

 __
 
• Static references are not a term officially used in MS Excel. Instead, such references may imply a type of reference that remains unchanged, similar to an **absolute reference**.
 
• Absolute references use **$** symbols to lock both the column and row, e.g., **$A$1**.
 
 
 
• **Mixed Reference**__
 __
 
• **Mixed references** in MS Excel lock either the **column** or the **row**, but not both.
 
• Examples of mixed references include **$A1** (column locked) or **A$1** (row locked).
 
• This type of reference is useful for creating formulas where partial adjustments are needed during copying.
 
 
 
• **Absolute Reference**__
 
 
• An **absolute reference** in MS Excel locks both the **row** and **column**, ensuring that the reference remains constant, no matter where the formula is copied.

questions.question: 5 What specific provision concerning the President of India is outlined in Article 59(3) of the Constitution of India?

__
 
• Article **59(3)** of the Constitution of India specifies provisions regarding the **salary, allowances, and privileges** of the President.
 
• The President of India is entitled to a **salary and allowances** that are determined by Parliament.
 
• The President's **official residence**, the Rashtrapati Bhavan, is also provided as part of the privileges.
 
• During their term, the President is entitled to **immunity** from criminal proceedings and cannot be summoned to appear in court.
 
• Article 59 ensures that the President's position is independent and dignified, safeguarding the office from any financial inconvenience.
 
• These provisions are vital to ensure the President can perform their constitutional duties without undue influence or hardship.
 
• Upon retirement, the President is entitled to a **pension**, as specified by Parliament.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Powers of the President**__

 __
 
• The President of India has extensive powers, including **executive, legislative, and judicial powers.**
 
• Some of these powers include the authority to appoint the **Prime Minister**, approve bills, and declare emergencies under Article 352, 356, and 360.
 
• The President also has the **power to grant pardons** under Article 72.
 
 
 
• **Election of the President**__
 __
 
• The President is elected through an **electoral college** consisting of elected members of Parliament and Legislative Assemblies.
 
• The election process is governed by Article **55** of the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Impeachment of the President**__
 
 
• The President can be removed through a process of **impeachment** under Article **61**.
 
• This process requires a majority in both Houses of Parliament and is conducted for **violation of the Constitution.**

questions.question: The complete sequencing of the human genome has marked the beginning of:
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Genomics**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Genomics** is the study of the entire set of genes (genome) of an organism, including their structure, function, and evolution.
 
• The completion of the **Human Genome Project** in 2003 marked the beginning of genomics.
 
• The **Human Genome Project** was a global scientific research initiative aimed at sequencing the entire human genome, consisting of approximately **3 billion DNA base pairs.**
 
• Genomics enables researchers to understand the **role of genes** in various biological processes, diseases, and traits.
 
• Applications of genomics include **personalized medicine, drug discovery, biotechnology, and agricultural improvements.**
 
• In personalized medicine, genomics helps identify **genetic markers** for diseases, enabling targeted treatments and preventive measures.
 
• Genomics also contributes to understanding **evolutionary biology** by comparing genomes across different species.
 
• It has paved the way for advanced technologies such as **CRISPR gene editing, transcriptomics, and proteomics.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Immunology**__

 __
 
• **Immunology** is the branch of biology that studies the immune system, its functions, and disorders.
 
• It focuses on understanding how the body defends itself against **pathogens** such as viruses, bacteria, and parasites.
 
• Applications of immunology include **vaccine development, immunotherapy, and diagnosing autoimmune diseases.**
 
• While immunology is crucial in healthcare, it is not directly related to genome sequencing.
 
 
 
• **Cytogenetics**__
 __
 
• **Cytogenetics** is the study of chromosomes, their structure, and their role in heredity and diseases.
 
• It involves techniques like **karyotyping** to detect chromosomal abnormalities such as Down syndrome and Turner syndrome.
 
• Cytogenetics is more focused on the physical aspects of chromosomes rather than whole-genome sequencing.
 
 
 
• **Structural Biology**__
 
 
• **Structural Biology** is the study of the molecular structure and dynamics of biological macromolecules like proteins and nucleic acids.
 
• It employs techniques such as **X-ray crystallography, NMR spectroscopy, and cryo-electron microscopy.**
 
• While structural biology contributes to understanding biological processes, it does not encompass the entire genome.

• The alluvial deposits in this region are a result of **continuous sedimentation** over millions of years.
 
• The plain covers a vast area, stretching across the states of **Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal, and Assam**.
 
• It is divided into three main sections: the **Punjab Plains, Ganga Plains, and Brahmaputra Plains**, each named after the dominant river system in the respective area.
 
• The region is densely populated due to its **fertile land, availability of water, and favorable climatic conditions**.
 
• The alluvial soil in the Northern Plain is rich in **minerals like potash and lime**, making it ideal for agriculture.

• **Rocky and elevated**__

• The Northern Plain, being formed by river deposits, is **flat and not rocky or elevated**.

questions.question: Which part of a Hindu temple serves as the innermost chamber for the primary deity?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Garbhagriha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Garbhagriha**, meaning "womb chamber," is the **innermost sanctum of a Hindu temple**.
 
• It is the place where the **main deity or idol** of the temple is housed and worshipped.
 
• The Garbhagriha is usually a small, dark chamber that is considered **highly sacred**.
 
• The deity housed within the Garbhagriha is regarded as the **focal point** of all temple rituals and worship.
 
• The design of the Garbhagriha often reflects a **symbolic representation** of the universe and cosmic energy.
 
• Access to the Garbhagriha is generally **restricted to priests**, emphasizing its sacred nature.
 
• It is often topped by a **Shikhara** (in North India) or a **Vimana** (in South India), which is a towering structure symbolizing a connection to the divine.
 
• In most cases, the Garbhagriha is oriented to the east, allowing the rising sun's rays to illuminate the deity during sunrise.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Shikhara**__

 __
 
• The **Shikhara** is the towering spire above the Garbhagriha in North Indian temples.
 
• It symbolizes **Mount Meru**, believed to be the center of the universe in Hindu cosmology.
 
• Shikharas are often ornately decorated and serve as a **visual cue** of the temple's sacred nature.
 
 
 
• **Jagati**__
 __
 
• The **Jagati** refers to the **platform** on which the temple is built.
 
• It provides a raised base, symbolizing the **separation of the sacred space** from the mundane world.
 
• The Jagati often serves as a circumambulatory path for devotees to walk around the temple in worship.
 
 
 
• **Kalasha**__
 
 
• The **Kalasha** is a decorative, often metal finial placed at the top of the temple's Shikhara or Vimana.
 
• It represents the **symbolic pot of nectar** and is considered an auspicious element in temple architecture.
 
• The Kalasha is often associated with fertility, abundance, and divine blessings.

questions.question: Which prominent Indian leader led the Bardoli Satyagraha of 1928, a major civil disobedience movement against increased land taxes?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Vallabhbhai Patel**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vallabhbhai Patel**, also known as the **‘Iron Man of India’**, was a prominent leader in the Indian freedom struggle.
 
• He led the **Bardoli Satyagraha of 1928**, a significant movement to protest against the **unjust increase in land revenue taxes** by the British authorities.
 
• The Satyagraha was conducted in the **Bardoli taluka of Gujarat**, where farmers were heavily burdened by a **30% hike in land revenue**.
 
• Under Patel's leadership, farmers refused to pay the increased taxes and launched a **non-violent resistance movement**.
 
• The movement was successful in forcing the British government to **roll back the increased revenue**, making it a landmark victory for civil disobedience.
 
• For his leadership in Bardoli, Vallabhbhai Patel earned the title of **Sardar**, which means ‘leader’ or ‘chief’.
 
• The Bardoli Satyagraha was a precursor to the larger Civil Disobedience Movement led by **Mahatma Gandhi**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi**__

 __
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi** was the leader of the **Indian National Movement** and a strong proponent of **non-violence** and **Satyagraha**.
 
• Although Gandhi was not directly involved in Bardoli, his principles of **Satyagraha** inspired Vallabhbhai Patel’s leadership.
 
• He led various other movements such as the **Salt March**, **Non-Cooperation Movement**, and **Quit India Movement**.
 
 
 
• **Bal Gangadhar Tilak**__
 __
 
• **Bal Gangadhar Tilak**, also known as **‘Lokmanya’**, was one of the earliest leaders of the Indian independence movement.
 
• He was not associated with the Bardoli Satyagraha but is known for his famous slogan, **"Swaraj is my birthright, and I shall have it."**
 
• Tilak was a strong advocate for **self-rule** and played a vital role in the **Swadeshi Movement**.
 
 
 
• **Jawaharlal Nehru**__
 
 
• **Jawaharlal Nehru** was India’s first **Prime Minister** and a prominent figure in the freedom struggle.
 
• He was not directly involved in the Bardoli Satyagraha but contributed significantly to other movements, including the **Civil Disobedience Movement** and **Quit India Movement**.
 
• He is known for his vision of a **modern, industrialized India** and for promoting the idea of **secularism and democracy**.
